status_reason: A new experiment built on Rensink, O'Regan & Clark's flicker paradigm and timing. Their Experiment 3 cued the changing object with a word; here the word names a depth plane (NEAR or FAR), is 75% valid, and the report is keyed. The main set uses 48 generated photograph pairs (each place photographed with a near and with a far change); drawn two-plane scenes remain as separate sets. Not a replication of any published result.

original.citation: Rensink, R. A., O'Regan, J. K., & Clark, J. J. (1997). To see or not to see: The need for attention to perceive changes in scenes. Psychological Science, 8(5), 368-373.
original.experiments: the flicker paradigm and Experiment 3's verbal cue, with the cue changed to a depth plane

assets.what: two-plane scene pairs, drawn at run time from a seed (no image files)

54 photograph pairs (A, A'): 27 places, each with a near-layer and a far-layer change; generated with an image model for this experiment (prompts and models in photos/spec.json), composited so A and A' differ only at the change (scripts/build_photo_pairs.py)
Atkinson Hyperlegible Regular and Bold (Braille Institute), used for the cue word and the report prompts

notes: Software verification only (tests and simulated sessions); no participant data. Four parameter sets: practice, main (75% valid), with neutral cues, and size-matched planes.
